title: Forest Fire in Sriparvata
subtitle: From Forest Ember to Crowned Flame
era: Kadamba consolidation after the Kanchi quarrel, c. 345-365 CE
region: Sriparvata forests, Banavasi, Chandravalli and the Pallava frontier
moral: Rebellion becomes statecraft only when it wins order.

sources.citation: Talagunda pillar inscription, vv. 13-22; Kielhorn, Epigraphia Indica 8 (1906)
sources.note: Primary account of the Sriparvata base, night attacks, taxes and Pallava recognition.

sources.citation: Chandravalli rock inscription of Mayurasharma; cited in Kamath, A Concise History of Karnataka (2001), p. 31
sources.note: Lists defeated or confronted powers in a royal proclamation.

sources.citation: Halasi copper plates of Kakusthavarma; J.F. Fleet, Indian Antiquary 6 (1877): 22-27; G.S. Gai (1996)
sources.note: Retrospective evidence for Mayurasharma's ashvamedha claims and brahmadeya gifts.

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a shadowed forest edge opening onto distant Pallava camps

dialogue.text: Hunted in Kanchi, hidden in Sriparvata, Mayurasharma now wages a forest war that forces the mighty Pallavas to crown his fury as a kingdom.

panels.shot: slow push-in from high forest canopy down to hidden ravine

dialogue.text: After the quarrel at Kanchi’s sacrifice halls, Mayurasharma vanished into the forests of Sriparvata, his wounded pride now shaping a new, harsher resolve.

panels.shot: medium close-up on Mayurasharma’s face lit by flickering firelight

dialogue.text: The student who once came to Kanchi for sacred learning now drew paths of ambush and tribute in the dust, treating the forest as his fortress and school of war.

panels.shot: wide shot of forest track with a small armed band emerging from shadows

dialogue.text: Talagunda remembers him taking shelter in Sriparvata’s woods, gathering men who knew every ridge and ravine better than the polished marble of Kanchi’s courts.

panels.shot: nighttime bird’s-eye shot over a small frontier village near forest edge

dialogue.text: From this shelter he began to levy tribute on nearby rulers and chiefs, not with royal seals, but with sudden arrivals at night and quiet demands at dawn.

panels.shot: medium shot at ground level of Mayurasharma and a trembling chieftain

dialogue.speaker: mayurasharma
dialogue.text: Your dues will no longer go only to Kanchi. The forest also has a lord.

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of a Pallava border camp in disarray

dialogue.text: Talagunda says he troubled Pallava camps from his forest base, appearing as a sudden storm at their frontier tents and vanishing before the full army could turn.

panels.shot: low-angle shot from inside a Pallava tent flap, looking out

dialogue.text: These were not set battles of the field, but cuts and slashes at the edges of empire, each raid a question thrown at Pallava pride.

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot showing multiple frontier landscapes

dialogue.text: Later, at Chandravalli, his scribes would recite a longer list—Traikutas, Abhiras, Sendrakas, Punnatas and others—names of neighbors claimed as cowed or confronted by this forest-born power.

panels.shot: tight focus on an inscription being chiseled into rock

dialogue.text: The Chandravalli record speaks with the pride of victory, yet the historian must hear in its bold lines both memory and exaggeration, both fact and crafted boast.

panels.shot: medium shot in a forest clearing with messengers arriving

dialogue.text: What began as a fugitive’s camp slowly hardened into a state’s first skeleton: streams of tribute, oaths of protection, and the quiet understanding that rule had changed hands.

panels.shot: sweeping wide shot of a Pallava council hall

dialogue.text: For the Pallavas, each report from Sriparvata was a thorn: a former student, now a rebel lord, refusing to be only a name in their list of punished offenders.

panels.shot: medium two-shot of a Pallava envoy and Mayurasharma

dialogue.text: Talagunda speaks of an end to this long harassment: the Pallava lords, faced with a stubborn fire they could not stamp out, accepted Mayurasharma as their friend and sovereign in his sphere.

panels.shot: close-up on hands exchanging a symbolic object

dialogue.speaker: mayurasharma
dialogue.text: Let it be known: the forest is no rebel’s den, but a kingdom.

panels.shot: grand wide shot of Banavasi landscape with early town structures

dialogue.text: With recognition came the work of order: Banavasi, once another forest-side settlement, became the beating heart of the Kadamba realm, binding tribute, justice and worship into one frame.

panels.shot: medium shot of Mayurasharma presiding over a land grant ceremony

dialogue.text: Kadamba records remember him as both warrior and patron, granting brahmadeya lands and using the tools of the very order that once humiliated him to now legitimize his own throne.

panels.shot: symbolic shot of a white horse near a sacrificial post (no violence)

dialogue.text: Later Halasi plates claim that he performed ashvamedha rites, embracing the highest symbols of sovereignty, declaring that a once-insulted student now strode the ritual path of emperors.

panels.shot: intimate close-up of Mayurasharma looking at an inscription pillar

dialogue.text: Yet the same pillar that praises his raids and taxes also speaks of a man who turned fury into structure, making the forest not just a refuge, but the root of a dynasty.

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot blending forest, town, and distant Pallava land

dialogue.text: His story reminds us that rebellion becomes statecraft not when swords strike hardest, but when a restless fire learns to govern, to tax, to grant, and to stand as an equal among powers.
